# Azure Cosmos DB

**Parity grade: B** · SDK `azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/data/azcosmos@v1.5.0` · last audited 2026-10-20 (`658ecc434`)

### Known gaps

- Throughput: physical partitions are modelled from RU only, ceil(RU/10000) of the offer (autoscale uses its maximum); the documented 50 GB storage term is not modelled, a lowered throughput shrinks the ranges at once (the service never merges partitions), range ids are always 0..N-1 (no split parents or ids), partition keys map to ranges by an even split of a SHA-256 hash space with 64-bit EPK bounds (the service uses MurmurHash3 over the encoded key), a cross-partition request charges its RU evenly across all partitions rather than by work done, and a shared database offer is partitioned by its total RU; burst capacity is a model of the documented 300 s idle bank spent at up to 3000 RU/s total per partition (applicability conditions unverified, not enforced for partitions already at 3000 RU/s or more); autoscale reports only its minimum, x-ms-cosmos-current-throughput is not exposed by azcosmos and is not emitted; serverless accounts are a single process-wide mode (--cosmosdb-serverless) with the 5000 RU/s container cap but no 50 GB storage limit; the replace between manual and autoscale is accepted on the data plane; minimum throughput is a flat 400 RU/s (not storage- or container-count-derived); Table API and metadata operations are not metered; the throughput error texts (min 400 manual / 1000 autoscale, steps of 100 / 1000, max 1,000,000) are from documented limits and the 429 text follows the task wording, not captured service responses
- IndexingPolicy: multi-key ORDER BY composite-index, excluded-path/scan and vector/full-text index enforcement exist (families.indexing, families.search); still open are spatial index validation and enforcement inside stored-procedure queries (the docs state neither); a single-key ORDER BY on a path the policy does not index is 400 (text from the Mongo-API troubleshooting page and Microsoft Q&A, same engine; the scan header does not bypass it), `id` and `_ts` are always indexed in consistent mode, and lazy mode is rejected with 400 because the index-policy page says new containers cannot select it (error text paraphrased, exemptions not modelled). Filter plus ORDER BY needs no composite index (the index-policy page: the query still succeeds, only RU cost differs) and the current page no longer requires vector paths in excludedPaths, so neither is enforced
- MultiRegion: regions, failoverPriority, multi-write and manual failover (ARM failoverPriorityChange) are modelled as account metadata over ONE physical store, so there is no replication lag, no regional endpoint, no automatic failover, no preferred-region routing and no write conflicts or conflicts feed; the data plane is one account, so the last ARM account written decides the topology; consistency levels other than a static session token are not modeled
- RequestCharge: an approximation of documented costs, not a metering of index and storage work
- SQL: ORDER BY combined with GROUP BY is accepted although the real service may reject it (the ORDER BY and GROUP BY reference pages, checked 2026-10-24, state neither a restriction nor an error text, so behaviour stays permissive); spatial functions are planar/haversine approximations with no Multi* geometry operations and no Geometry-mode (planar metre) semantics; ST_ISVALIDDETAILED reasons beyond the unclosed-ring text are paraphrased; VectorDistance is exact (no approximate index, no quantization error, dataType only validated) and FullTextScore tokenization has no stemming (families.search); unsupported functions are a 400 parse error
- ItemOperations: the all-versions-and-deletes feed keeps only the newest 10000 versions per container and ignores the continuous-backup retention window; pre/post triggers fire for create, upsert, replace and delete only (the triggers REST page: "creation, deletion, and replacement of a document"; the patch REST page has no trigger header and azcosmos transactional batch has no trigger option), so PATCH and batch run none; stored procedure callbacks run synchronously, and a stored procedure runs on a private copy of its container without the backend lock, committing only if the container was not written meanwhile (up to 4 tries, then under the write lock), so a long script no longer stalls other containers but a busy container can fall back to the lock; there is no server-side bulk operation (the SDKs implement bulk client-side over batches and point operations)
- Containers: geospatialConfig is stored and echoed only (no planar Geometry behaviour); vectorEmbeddingPolicy and fullTextPolicy are validated and enforced (families.search); computed properties are not used for index selection; the replace-time error text for a changed unique key policy is unverified
- TableAPI: a $batch answers a single bare query (point retrieve or entity-collection query with $filter/$top/$select, 200 feed in the part; the docs show only the point retrieve, and a query part carries no continuation headers because the Table API here pages nothing), but several changesets (the service processes the first and rejects the rest with 400; here the whole request is 400 because the rejection response shape is undocumented), is 400; the 4 MiB payload limit is enforced as 400 InvalidInput with no documented service error code; Table API responses carry no per-operation request charge or continuation beyond what pkgs/odatatable provides
- ResourceTokens: a document permission matches by document id across all partition keys (ids repeat across keys; the permission docs define no partition scoping for a document resource, while container permissions with resourcePartitionKey are already restricted to that key); permissions on stored procedures, triggers, UDFs and attachments are rejected rather than modelled; a permission left pointing at a deleted container simply grants nothing; the minimum x-ms-documentdb-expiry-seconds is unverified (docs give only the 3600 default and the 18000 maximum)
